nodes.name: 02.1 Encode PDF for OCR
nodes.notes: REUSED VERBATIM from examples/n8n/digitax_invoice_intake.json (same node id/parameters -- jsCode is unchanged, so it stays covered by test_ocr_nodes_reused_verbatim_from_intake_workflow). Do not modify the extraction logic here -- see the workflow-level note on why binaryPropertyName stays "data". Cloud lane only -- the local lane has its own identical copy, "02.1L Encode PDF for local OCR", so the two provider paths stay technically independent end to end. onError: "continueErrorOutput" added 2026-08-11 (same pattern as "02.5 Parse OCR/LLM output"): getBinaryDataBuffer can throw for reasons unrelated to the OCR service itself (e.g. a missing/corrupted binary attachment), and this must never crash the run unhandled -- it now routes to "02.4 Handle OCR service failure" instead.

parameters.jsCode:
return items.map(item => {
  return {
    json: {
      geminiRequest: {
        contents: [
          {
            parts: [
              {
                inline_data: {
                  mime_type: 'application/pdf',
                  data: item.json.pdfBase64
                }
              },
              {
                text: `Extract invoice header information from this PDF and return JSON only.

Extraction rules:
1. Distinguish seller (the party issuing/sending the invoice) from buyer
   (the party the invoice is addressed to) using only the document's own
   labels and layout -- for example "Rechnungssteller"/"Von"/"Lieferant"
   typically marks the seller, and "Rechnungsempfaenger"/"An"/"Kunde"/
   "Bill To" typically marks the buyer. Do not assume in advance which
   company is the buyer or seller; read it from the document only.
2. Assign each VAT ID to whichever party it is printed next to on the
   document -- as "VAT-ID (Seller)" or "VAT-ID (Buyer)" accordingly.
3. If a VAT ID's owner (seller or buyer) cannot be determined with
   confidence from the document alone, return "not found" for that field
   rather than guessing.
4. All monetary amounts are plain numbers -- no currency symbol, no
   thousands separator, dot as decimal separator (e.g. 119.00, not
   "119,00" or "EUR 119,00").
5. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD.
6. "Line Items" is an array with one entry per distinct line/position in
   the invoice's line-item table; an empty array if no such table is
   visible.
7. Output JSON only. Do not add explanations or markdown fences.

Return exactly one JSON object with these fields:
{
  "Invoice No": "string",
  "Invoice Date": "string",
  "Type Code": "string",
  "Currency": "string",
  "VAT-ID (Seller)": "string",
  "VAT-ID (Buyer)": "string",
  "Tax ID (Seller)": "string",
  "Tax ID (Buyer)": "string",
  "Name (Seller)": "string",
  "Address (Seller)": "string",
  "Zip (Seller)": "string",
  "City (Seller)": "string",
  "Country (Seller)": "string",
  "Name (Buyer)": "string",
  "Address (Buyer)": "string",
  "Zip (Buyer)": "string",
  "City (Buyer)": "string",
  "Country (Buyer)": "string",
  "Supply Description": "string",
  "Delivery Date": "string",
  "Period Start": "string",
  "Period End": "string",
  "Net Total": "number",
  "Tax Basis": "number",
  "Tax Amount": "number",
  "Gross Total": "number",
  "Payable Amount": "number",
  "Charge Total": "number",
  "Allowance Total": "number",
  "Prepaid Amount": "number",
  "Rounding Amount": "number",
  "Line Items": [{"Description": "string", "Quantity": "number", "Net Amount": "number", "VAT Rate": "number"}]
}

If a text field is missing or illegible, return "not found". If a number
field is missing or illegible, return null.`
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  };
});

nodes.name: 02.2 Build OCR/LLM request
nodes.notes: CORRECTED from digitax_invoice_intake.json (2026-08-10, final-demo-ui round): the original prompt hardcoded the expected buyer company, its approved addresses, and its VAT ID -- master data the OCR step must never see, since it would let the model return the "expected" answer instead of what the document actually says, silently defeating the downstream ORG-001 comparison. This node now extracts using only document-visible labels/layout; master data is used exclusively downstream, in the control logic, after extraction. digitax_invoice_intake.json itself is intentionally left with its original (uncorrected) prompt, since that file remains a historical, untouched reference. tests/test_n8n_flow1b_workflow.py has a dedicated test asserting no organization name/address/VAT-ID reference value ever appears in this prompt text again.

1. Distinguish seller (the party issuing/sending the invoice) from buyer
   (the party the invoice is addressed to) using only the document's own
   labels and layout -- for example "Rechnungssteller"/"Von"/"Lieferant"
   typically marks the seller, and "Rechnungsempfaenger"/"An"/"Kunde"/

2. Assign each VAT ID to whichever party it is printed next to on the
   document -- as "VAT-ID (Seller)" or "VAT-ID (Buyer)" accordingly.
3. If a VAT ID's owner (seller or buyer) cannot be determined with
   confidence from the document alone, return "not found" for that field
   rather than guessing.
4. All monetary amounts are plain numbers -- no currency symbol, no
   thousands separator, dot as decimal separator (e.g. 119.00, not
   "119,00" or "EUR 119,00").
5. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD.
6. "Line Items" is an array with one entry per distinct line/position in
   the invoice's line-item table; an empty array if no such table is
   visible.
7. Output JSON only. Do not add explanations or markdown fences.

Return exactly one JSON object with these fields:
{
  "Invoice No": "string",
  "Invoice Date": "string",
  "Type Code": "string",
  "Currency": "string",
  "VAT-ID (Seller)": "string",
  "VAT-ID (Buyer)": "string",
  "Tax ID (Seller)": "string",
  "Tax ID (Buyer)": "string",
  "Name (Seller)": "string",
  "Address (Seller)": "string",
  "Zip (Seller)": "string",
  "City (Seller)": "string",
  "Country (Seller)": "string",
  "Name (Buyer)": "string",
  "Address (Buyer)": "string",
  "Zip (Buyer)": "string",
  "City (Buyer)": "string",
  "Country (Buyer)": "string",
  "Supply Description": "string",
  "Delivery Date": "string",
  "Period Start": "string",
  "Period End": "string",
  "Net Total": "number",
  "Tax Basis": "number",
  "Tax Amount": "number",
  "Gross Total": "number",
  "Payable Amount": "number",
  "Charge Total": "number",
  "Allowance Total": "number",
  "Prepaid Amount": "number",
  "Rounding Amount": "number",

}

If a text field is missing or illegible, return "not found". If a number
field is missing or illegible, return null.`;

const profile = $('01.9 Resolve AI execution profile').item.json.resolvedProfile;

return items.map(item => ({
  json: {
    localRequest: {
      model: profile.modelId,
      temperature: 0,
      messages: [
        {
          role: 'user',
          content: [
            { type: 'text', text: EXTRACTION_PROMPT },
            {
              type: 'image_url',
              image_url: { url: `data:image/png;base64,${item.json.pngBase64}` },
            },
          ],
        },
      ],
    },
  },
}));

nodes.name: 02.3L Run OCR/LLM extraction (local)
nodes.notes: No credential/auth by default -- targets a developer-configured local OpenAI-compatible endpoint (LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL), which is typically unauthenticated in dev. If your local endpoint needs an API key, add an Authorization header sourced from an environment expression here; never hardcode one. Bounded retry is shorter than the cloud lane's (3 tries vs 5) since a local dev endpoint should fail fast rather than mask a real unavailability -- see "01.9 Resolve AI execution profile" for the pre-flight configured-availability check that avoids even attempting this call when LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL is unset.

nodes.name: 05.1 Human review - standard
nodes.notes: Phase 1b ends here: routed for standard-priority human review. No automated approval, booking, payment, or supplier communication.

nodes.name: 05.2 Human review - prioritized
nodes.notes: Phase 1b ends here: routed for prioritized human review (klaerung_erforderlich, or a nicht_pruefbar not_reliable-extraction outcome from ORG-001 itself). No automated approval, booking, payment, or supplier communication.

nodes.name: 05.3 Human review - technical
nodes.notes: Explicit technical-failure route -- does not depend on the unknown-value fallback. Reached for missing upload, unknown organization profile, unresolved AI execution profile, local/cloud OCR service failure, or OCR output parse failure. parameters.content:
## 01.6-01.11 Organization + AI-profile resolution
Organization master-data profile lookup (concept), then AI execution
profile resolution: the browser sends only a stable profile ID
(local-default / cloud-gemini). An unknown ID or an unconfigured local
provider fails safely to nicht_pruefbar/technical_review -- never a
silent default to cloud, never a silent local-to-cloud fallback.

## 02 Intake and normalization -- two technically separate lanes
n8n performs the selected OCR/LLM extraction only. Cloud lane (y=0):
unchanged Gemini path. Local lane (y=460, below): configurable local
OpenAI-compatible endpoint, no model bundled or auto-downloaded. Both
lanes converge on 02.7 Normalize invoice with an identical canonical
invoice/fieldEvidence/aiMeta shape, then submitted to the authoritative
Phase 1 API for control evaluation (see 03 DigiTax controls).

## 02L Local AI extraction (concept)
OpenAI-compatible endpoint via LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL/LOCAL_LLM_MODEL.
Unavailable/unconfigured -> nicht_pruefbar/technical_review, never a
silent fallback to cloud.

## 03 DigiTax controls
The authoritative Phase 1 API evaluates all controls
(ORG-001 and every other control) via
POST /v1/invoices/process-extracted -- the same
catalog/executor Flow 1a uses. n8n performs no
control logic of its own.

## 04 Control report and routing
Adds AI-selection audit fields: processingPath, aiExecutionProfile,
aiProvider, modelId, modelVersion, processingLocation, promptVersion,
fallbackUsed. No secrets or internal URLs are ever included.

## VERSION INFO
Workflow: DigiTax | Invoice Phase 1 | Flow 1b | PDF OCR/LLM Concept | v0.3.0
Status: concept (inactive, credentials pending -- NOT part of the demo).
Workflow remains inactive/concept-level and ends before human decision.
Boundary: plain PDF upload -> resolve AI execution profile -> local OR
cloud OCR/LLM extraction (n8n) -> control evaluation (authoritative
Phase 1 API) -> human review handoff (never approval, booking, payment,
or supplier communication)
AI selection (since v0.2.0): browser sends only a stable profile ID
(local-default / cloud-gemini); server/n8n resolves provider, model, and
endpoint. No silent local-to-cloud fallback; unknown profile or
unconfigured local provider fails safely to nicht_pruefbar/
technical_review. Both lanes converge on one canonical invoice contract.
Control contract (since v0.3.0): n8n performs the selected OCR/LLM
extraction only; the authoritative Phase 1 API evaluates all controls
(ORG-001 rule_version 1.0.0, threshold 0.70, and every other control) via
POST /v1/invoices/process-extracted -- see
facturx/phase1/controls/catalog.py and executor.py::evaluate_org_001.
Source: digitax_invoice_phase1_flow1b_pdf_ocr_concept_v0_3_0.json

nodes.name: 02.1L-b Render PDF page as PNG (local render helper)
nodes.notes: CONCEPT, added for the local AI lane only: most local OpenAI-compatible vision endpoints (verified against LM Studio) reject a raw PDF passed as image_url and require an actual rendered image -- unlike Gemini's cloud API, which accepts the PDF directly in the cloud lane (unchanged). Calls a small dev-only render helper (examples/n8n/scripts/pdf_render_service.py) over LOCAL_PDF_RENDER_URL, resolved purely from environment settings -- never a hardcoded deployment host. Not bundled or auto-started; must already be running. onError: continueErrorOutput routes to the existing 02.4L failure handler, same as the other local-lane HTTP call.

main.node: 02.1L-b Render PDF page as PNG (local render helper)
